 Isaiah Hartenstein notched 21 points (9-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 16 rebounds, six assists and one steal in Friday’s loss to the Clippers.
 After scoring no more than seven points in any of Oklahoma City’s first five games in November, Hartenstein has scored at least 20 in two straight games. He was outstanding against the Clippers, shooting 90 percent from the field and providing excellent value in points, rebounds and assists. Providing top-100 fantasy value, Hartenstein is rostered in 84 percent of Yahoo leagues. Given Oklahoma City’s frontcourt injuries, those rostering Hartenstein would be better served holding on to him than entertaining a trade after the last two games. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Isaiah Hartenstein

 Center-Forward 
 #55 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Isaiah Hartenstein accumulated 20 points (10-of-14 FGs), 11 rebounds, six assists and two steals in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 After totaling 19 points in Oklahoma City’s first five games of November, Hartenstein recorded his first 20-point game of the season on Wednesday. The negative for iHart was the turnovers, of which he was responsible for six. A few of the turnovers were due to offensive fouls, so there isn’t much to worry about there. Rostered in 83 percent of Yahoo leagues, Hartenstein is providing top-100 fantasy value, slightly better than his ADP. 
 Isaiah Hartenstein 
 OKC 
 Center-Forward 
 #55 
 Isaiah Hartenstein amassed 10 points (3-of-8 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds and three steals in Saturday’s loss to the Rockets. 
 With Chet Holmgren (knee) out for at least 8-10 weeks, the Thunder will rely even more on Hartenstein, Jaylin Williams (3/4/1/1) and Aday Mara (seven points, nine rebounds, three assists and four blocks) in the post. Of the three, Hartenstein is the safest option for fantasy managers, which is why he’s rostered in over 80 percent of Yahoo leagues. 
 Chet Holmgren 
 OKC 
 Center-Forward 
 #7 
 According to ESPN’s Tim MacMahon, Chet Holmgren (knee) will be sidelined for at least 8-10 weeks. 
 According to MacMahon, Holmgren underwent a biological treatment on Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear in his right knee. With Jalen Williams (ankle/fibula) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) facing extended absences, and given Holmgren’s injury history, fantasy managers should expect the Thunder to be very cautious with his rehab process. Kenrich Williams should remain in the starting lineup for the foreseeable future, and Aday Mara’s playing time should increase. Also, Holmgren’s absence raises Isaiah Hartenstein’s fantasy ceiling. 
 Isaiah Hartenstein 
 OKC 
 Center-Forward 
 #55 
 Isaiah Hartenstein accounted for 15 points (6-of-7 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), 13 rebounds and three assists in Monday’s win over the Suns. 
 With Chet Holmgren (knee) sitting out Monday’s game, Hartenstein was the lone 7-footer in the Thunder starting lineup. He recorded his second double-double in as many nights, and iHart’s ability to play both games of Oklahoma City’s back-to-back is encouraging. He appeared in 47 games last season, and injuries also contributed to Hartenstein’s minutes dropping by more than three per game. He’s looked healthy so far, which is critical with the Thunder losing Jalen Williams (ankle/leg) for the season on Sunday. 
 Chet Holmgren 
 OKC 
 Center-Forward 
 #7 
 Chet Holmgren (knee) is out for Monday’s game against the Suns. 
 Holmgren is dealing with right patellar tendonitis. Isaiah Hartenstein stepped up with 12 points and 12 rebounds in the win over the Clippers Sunday while Holmgren had a relatively quiet game with 10 points and four rebounds. Hartenstein should see even more usage with Holmgren out Monday against the Suns. 
 Isaiah Hartenstein 
 OKC 
 Center-Forward 
 #55 
 Isaiah Hartenstein recorded 12 points (5-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 12 rebounds, one assist and one steal in Sunday’s win over the Clippers. 
 After recording two underwhelming stat lines in Oklahoma City’s first two games of the season, Hartenstein posted a double-double on Sunday. His play helped offset Chet Holmgren’s quiet night at the office (10 points, four rebounds, one steal, one block and two three-pointers), helping push Oklahoma City’s record to 3-0. Hartenstein also played 27 minutes, an encouraging number given his limited minutes last season. 
 Aday Mara 
 OKC 
 Center 
 Aday Mara provided a boost off the bench with 10 points (4-of-5 FGs), four rebounds, one assist and three blocks against the Pacers on Tuesday. 
 Mara came off the bench with Isaiah Hartenstein making his preseason debut, but he was still able to make a solid impact in his 19 minutes. Mara has been productive during the preseason, and with Chet Holmgren (quad) and Jaylin Williams (heel) having been sidelined for the preseason so far, there is a chance Mara ends up playing a large role early on behind Isaiah Hartenstein. It’s a situation worth monitoring with the regular season set to start in just one week. 
 Aday Mara 
 OKC 
 Center 
 Aday Mara produced 22 points (10-of-10 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), six rebounds, two assists and one block in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Bucks. 
 With Isaiah Hartenstein sitting out a second straight preseason game, Mara started alongside projected starters Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Cason Wallace, and Jalen Williams on Wednesday. The rookie looked very comfortable in that role, meshing well with the Thunder playmakers in the two-man game. Mara didn’t miss a shot from the field, and Oklahoma City posted a +22.5 net rating when he was on the court. How valuable the rookie is in redraft leagues will depend on Hartenstein and Chet Holmgren’s health, with iHart limited to 47 regular-season games last season. 
 Isaiah Hartenstein 
 OKC 
 Center-Forward 
 #55 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Isaiah Hartenstein will sign a new three-year deal with the Oklahoma City Thunder. 
 Hartenstein’s reported deal will keep him under contract with OKC through the 2028-29 season. His new contract allows the Thunder to keep their starting center and a key piece from their 2024-25 championship team. He’s coming off a season in which he averaged 9.2 points, 9.4 rebounds and 3.5 assists per game. Hartenstein’s fantasy value can be tricky to gauge, as he’s missed at least 25 regular-season games in each of his two seasons in OKC. However, he’s a nightly double-double threat with playmaking ability that could be a useful piece for fantasy managers. 
 Jaylin Williams 
 OKC 
 Forward 
 #6 
 Jaylin Williams recorded 11 points (5-of-9 FGs), 10 rebounds, four assists and one three-pointer in Saturday’s Game 7 loss to the Spurs. 
 Williams shone in Game 7, recording his first double-double of these playoffs. Given the struggles of Chet Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein (seven points, five rebounds and one steal), JayWill’s production was one reason why the Thunder had a chance late. Williams has not been a consistent option for fantasy managers during his time in Oklahoma City, but that could change next season. Hartenstein has a team option worth $28.5 million, while new deals for Holmgren and Jalen Williams will begin. The salary cap situation could make JayWill someone whom the Thunder have to rely on more in 2026-27.

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished Friday’s loss to the Clippers with 40 points (15-of-26 FGs, 8-of-11 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
 Gilgeous-Alexander finished with his third 40-point game of the season, but he wishes he’d scored 42 instead of 40. The two-time MVP’s shot as time expired missed the mark, resulting in a 113-112 Clippers victory. After shooting a combined 17-of-42 in two losses to the Trail Blazers, Gilgeous-Alexander was much more efficient on Friday, shooting well over 50 percent from the field. He could be in for another big night to end the week, as the Thunder visit the Kings on Sunday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Keaton Wagler produced 14 points (4-of-7 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), two rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
 After reaching double figures in each of his first five games, Wagler totaled 13 points on 4-of-13 shooting in the Clippers’ first two games of November. The rookie has gotten back on track, having scored at least 11 points in four straight games. Wagler remains a deep-league option in redraft formats, while dynasty league managers should be excited for the rookie guard’s future.

 Derrick Jones Jr. accounted for 14 points (5-of-10 FGs), five rebounds, one steal, four blocks and four three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
 Thanks mainly to the three-pointers and defensive stats, Jones has been close to a top-100 player in nine-cat formats. Against the Thunder, he shot 4-of-7 from beyond the arc and recorded five “stocks” in 29 minutes. This was Jones’ fourth game this season with at least two three-pointers, one steal and one block. Managers needing help in those categories should consider adding Jones ahead of Sunday’s game against the Hornets.

 Brook Lopez accumulated 26 points (11-of-21 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
 After coming off the bench in the Clippers’ first six games, Lopez is approaching the point where he needs to be rostered in 12-team leagues. He’s scored at least 20 points in three of the last four games, with Friday’s total being a season high. Add in the rebounds and three-pointers, and this was a good night for those rostering the veteran center. Isaiah Jackson (5/3/3 with one block), who began the season as the starter, should be rostered only in very deep leagues. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Darius Garland finished Friday’s win over the Thunder with 24 points (8-of-17 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, seven assists, one block and three three-pointers.
 After being outscored 40-25 in the third quarter, Garland and the Clippers did what needed to be done down the stretch to win the 113-112 thriller. The Clippers’ starting point guard had the game’s biggest shot: a layup through contact and an ensuing free throw with 50.4 seconds left to take the lead for good. Even with the occasional struggles with turnovers, Garland is providing top-100 fantasy value through 11 games. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 After a really bad game against the Magic, Sabonis bounced back and went back to his usual self against the Blazers. He looked healthier in this game, which is a good sign. The efficiency has still been good, but it is starting to come down from his super-hot start. He still puts up good counting stats which is why you have Sabonis in the first place.
